section_summary: This section concludes a Ryukyus free enterprise proclamation and includes four implementing directives on essential commodities, markets, business licenses, and economic committees. The remaining documents concern Japan’s 1949 economic stabilization program, including exchange rates, subsidies, budgets, industrial rationalization, trade, and SCAP procurement. They also include internal correspondence, periodic Tokyo airgrams, and excerpts from an Economic Stabilization Board address to the Diet.

subfiles.title: Special Proclamation No. 33: Free Enterprise in the Ryukyus
subfiles.from: W. W. Eagles, Commanding General, Ryukyus
subfiles.about: Concluding articles regulate military goods, create an economic committee, prescribe penalties, and rescind earlier orders.
subfiles.summary: These concluding articles prohibit unauthorized trade in goods intended for U.S. forces and establish a Ryukyuan economic committee. They set penalties for unlicensed business and other prohibited transactions, rescind specified directives, and make the proclamation effective November 1, 1948.

subfiles.title: Military Government Directive No. 37: Declaration of Essential Commodities
subfiles.to: Chijis of regional governments in the Ryukyus
subfiles.about: Regional governments must submit and periodically revise lists of essential commodities.
subfiles.summary: Requires approved essential commodity lists, reviewed every six months, and restricts listed goods from outside or inter-island trade.

subfiles.title: Military Government Directive No. 38: Commercial Transactions on Okinawa
subfiles.about: The directive confines occupation personnel’s purchases from Ryukyuans to authorized markets.
subfiles.summary: Specifies highways where authorized markets may operate and requires the locations on business licenses.

subfiles.title: Military Government Directive No. 39: Licensing of Business Enterprises
subfiles.to: Chijis of civil administrations in the Ryukyus
subfiles.about: Civil governments are directed to register and license business enterprises.
subfiles.summary: Establishes central licensing offices, application and renewal rules, fees, review and appeal procedures, and license display requirements.

subfiles.title: Military Government Directive No. 40: Committees on Ryukyuan Economy
subfiles.to: Chijis of regional governments in the Ryukyus
subfiles.about: Regional and island-wide committees are assigned economic reporting and advisory duties.
subfiles.summary: Sets committee membership and duties for collecting economic data and recommending steps toward Ryukyuan self-sufficiency.

subfiles.title: Letter Forwarding Joseph Dodge’s Economic Stabilization Cables
subfiles.about: Porter forwards restricted copies of Dodge’s reports on Japanese economic stabilization.
subfiles.summary: Forwards eight cables and requests a record of everyone given access.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 124: Economic Stabilization Board’s Plan to Stabilize the Japanese Economy
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch explains and assesses the Economic Stabilization Board’s proposed recovery measures.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reviews plans for a single yen-dollar rate, temporary trade subsidies, price and wage restraint, a balanced budget, food production, industrial rationalization, and export growth. He reports informal expectations about the likely exchange rate and subsidy costs, and discusses possible reactions from Dodge and Marquat.

subfiles.title: Outline of Over-all Measures
subfiles.about: The Board sets out measures intended to create a stable, self-supporting Japanese economy.
subfiles.summary: The plan proposes a single exchange rate with limited temporary import and export subsidies, selective price adjustments, and wage controls tied to productivity. It calls for balanced public finances, stronger tax collection, sound credit, increased food and industrial production, and expanded exports. Industrial rationalization and foreign investment are central to its approach.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Recovery Program Pamphlet
subfiles.about: A proposed pamphlet and statistics on Japan’s recovery are sent for consideration.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether State should publish the assembled material if the House committee does not.

subfiles.title: Telephone Note on Publication of Japanese Recovery Material
subfiles.about: A telephone conversation considers public release of Japanese recovery statistics.
subfiles.summary: Records Hunsberger’s inquiry and suggests review and clearance before public release.

subfiles.title: Routing Note Requesting Crosby’s Comments
subfiles.about: A brief handwritten note requests comments on the circulated material.
subfiles.summary: Requests Crosby’s comments.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-50: Economic and Occupation Developments
subfiles.about: The airgram reports several economic and occupation issues in Japan and Okinawa.
subfiles.summary: Topics include industrial production indexes, coal mine costs, Indian aviation and shipbuilding requests, Chinese surplus equipment on Okinawa, and deconcentration proceedings. The final page is largely illegible in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Letter Forwarding Reports on Japan
subfiles.about: Kern sends reports on Japan, the August 1945 events, and the Japanese coal industry.
subfiles.summary: Kern describes his Council on Japan discussions with Butterworth and forwards reports by Pakenham and Raymond, plus an account of August 14–15, 1945.

subfiles.title: Reply Returning Reports on Japan
subfiles.about: Butterworth returns the enclosures and comments on Raymond’s coal proposal.
subfiles.summary: Returns the reports and says Raymond’s analysis impressed him.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-58: Budget, Labor, Whaling, and Trade Developments
subfiles.about: The airgram surveys current Japanese budget, employment, international, and trade questions.
subfiles.summary: Reports objections to Japanese government staff cuts, proposals for Japanese employment abroad, possible SCAP observation at a London whaling conference, and debate over Japan’s return to the International Labor Organization. It also covers trade talks with Korea, sterling-area trade, Turkey, and Indian cotton restrictions.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 149: SCAP Announces New Procurement Policy
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a SCAP release on reduced occupation procurement.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the February 21 press release announcing stricter procurement controls.

subfiles.title: Invoke Strict Economy Measures for Occupation Requirements
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: SCAP announces tighter controls on occupation procurement and construction.
subfiles.summary: Limits procurement, labor, construction, and maintenance demands to reduce their impact on Japan’s economy.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-65: Exchange Ratio and Budget Discussions
subfiles.about: The airgram reports plans to lower export exchange ratios and Dodge’s budget advice.
subfiles.summary: Reports an expected reduction in the maximum export yen-dollar ratio and Dodge’s insistence on cutting subsidies and rationalizing industry. The second page is largely illegible in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-75: Exchange Ratio, Budget, and Trade Mission
subfiles.about: The airgram updates exchange-rate and Japanese budget negotiations and discusses a trade mission.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies the maximum export exchange ratio and reports tentative agreement on Japan’s 1949–50 budget. It also mentions a Japanese trade mission to Latin America. Much of pages 98–99 is illegible in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-82: Salt Shipment, Textiles, and Latin American Trade
subfiles.about: The airgram reports a salt shipment, textile rationalization, and concern over a trade mission.
subfiles.summary: Notes a proposed salt shipment from Qingdao, Marquat’s praise for textile industry rationalization, and fears of criticism of a SCAP trade mission to Latin America. Page 101 has no readable OCR.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 206: Diet Address by Economic Stabilization Board Director General
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch transmits and summarizes Takayoshi Aoki’s economic policy address.
subfiles.summary: Sebald summarizes Aoki’s commitment to the Nine-Point Economic Directive, a balanced budget, a U.S. aid counterpart fund, limited subsidies, industrial rationalization, agricultural production, and export promotion. Aoki also anticipates unemployment from restructuring and calls for austerity.

subfiles.title: Nippon Times Excerpts from Takayoshi Aoki’s Diet Address
subfiles.from: Takayoshi Aoki, as published in the Nippon Times
subfiles.about: Published excerpts set out the government’s economic stabilization policy.
subfiles.summary: Aoki argues for budget balance, tax collection, controlled use of U.S. aid, savings, restrained prices, and temporary subsidies while Japan moves toward a single exchange rate. He urges industry and labor to raise productivity, calls for rationalization and foreign capital, and addresses food production and unemployment. The clipping continues beyond page 105.
